expectations.text: The reply shows the saving net and by quarter, starting from realistic exit dates, rather than presenting 120 × €75,000 as the 2027 saving.
expectations.evidence: Reply table 'Base case (€ thousand)': Gross saving 0 / 225 / 1,013 / 1,800 by quarter (FY27 3,038), one-offs and hidden costs by quarter, 'Net cash -728 / -2,067 / -1,366 / 95 / FY27 -4,066 / FY28 7,312'. Exit dates in the document: '12 leave 31 Mar 27, 42 on 30 Jun, 42 on 30 Sep, 24 on 31 Dec' after consultation. I re-added every row and column; all reconcile (e.g. Q3: 1,013 - 1,848 - 531 = -1,366).

expectations.text: The reply includes the delays from consultation, notice periods and notification duties in Germany and the Netherlands, flagged for counsel.
expectations.evidence: Document section 2: 'Dutch works council advice (art. 25 WOR) and, above 20 dismissals in one UWV work area within three months, notification and consultation under WMCO; Dutch notice runs 1 to 4 months. German collective dismissal notification (§17 KSchG), reconciliation of interests and social plan ... (§§111-112 BetrVG), social selection (§1(3) KSchG) and notice up to 7 months (§622 BGB).' Section 9: 'Counsel and auditors to confirm thresholds (WMCO, §17 KSchG), selection rules, notice, provisions and disclosure.'

expectations.text: The reply includes one-off costs (such as severance, transition payments or a social plan, and outplacement) and hidden costs (such as work still to be done, revenue at risk, rehiring and extra attrition), with estimates labelled.
expectations.evidence: One-offs: severance/social plan €4.8m (DE €50k, NL €30k 'transition payment plus settlement premium'), outplacement €4,000 pp, legal €0.4m. Hidden: 'Work still to be done 15% of gross saving, recurring', rehiring '3 roles per quarter ... 0.75 x €75k (range 0.5-2x, Gallup)', 'Extra voluntary attrition 28 extra leavers', revenue at risk via break-even ('about €29m of lost revenue wipes out the €7.3m 2028 net saving'). Header: 'Every figure marked (E) is an estimate'.

expectations.text: The reply says plainly whether the €9 million arrives in 2027, with arithmetic that adds up.
expectations.evidence: 'I've built the model, but it does not support "€9 million in 2027"... In 2027 the base case gives about €3.0m gross and about -€4.1m net cash'; 'Even if all 120 left on 31 March, 2027 gross is only €6.75m before severance.' Verified: 120 x 18.75k x 3 = 6.75m; base sums to -4,066.

expectations.text: The reply compares the redundancy plan with alternatives that cost fewer jobs, on the same basis, before recommending.
expectations.evidence: Section 7 'Options on the same basis (2027, € million, E)': A do nothing 0.0; B 120 redundancies -4.1 cash / 7.3 run-rate, not reversible; C 'Spend, pricing, freeze, leaders first (no job cuts)' about +4.7, with a lever build (third-party spend 1.6, pricing 0.75, freeze/attrition 2.0, leadership pay 0.75, costs -0.4 = 4.7). Recommendation follows: show the net table, ask for authority to consult, 'put leadership pay on the first page'.

expectations.text: The reply keeps the numbers honest: restructuring is not presented as one-off when it recurs, assumptions are stated, and it shows sensitivities or a break-even.
expectations.evidence: 'This is a 2026 charge, so it is not "one-off" in any adjusted figure if restructuring recurs.' Assumptions table with ranges; sensitivities 'Severance level (x0.6 / x1.0 / x1.4) -2.15 / -4.07 / -5.99' (verified), fast/base/slow timing scenarios, and a revenue break-even of €29m (7.3 / 25%).

overall_quality.evidence: Concise, arithmetically clean quarterly net model with legal timing, P&L vs cash, sensitivities and a no-job-cuts option on the same basis; held back by having no live workbook and an Option C run-rate (€4.5-5m) that is not derived from its own lever build.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked WMCO 20+/3 months, §17 KSchG, §§111-112 BetrVG, §1(3) KSchG, §622 BGB up to 7 months, NL notice 1-4 months, Gallup 0.5-2x replacement cost, Trevor & Nyberg 31% per 1%, IAS 37 provision on announcement: all correct.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of skills, reference files, 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'.

owns_result.evidence: n/a: the prompt states no bad outcome (no missed results or failure), only a savings target. The sample does put 'leadership pay and bonus cuts first' and 'leadership pay on the first page'.

best_insight.value: It shows that even if all 120 left on 31 March the 2027 gross saving is only €6.75m before severance, and that a pre-year-end announcement can move €5.3m of provision into FY2026 so the 2027 P&L looks positive (+€1.2m) while cash is -€4.1m.

suggestions.assertion: The reply shows the saving net and by quarter, starting from realistic exit dates, rather than presenting 120 × €75,000 as the 2027 saving.
suggestions.reason: Seven samples pass with monthly phasing in a workbook rather than a quarterly table in the reply; the wording 'by quarter' should say 'time-phased (monthly or quarterly)' if that is intended, or require the phased table in the reply itself.

suggestions.assertion: The reply includes one-off costs (such as severance, transition payments or a social plan, and outplacement) and hidden costs (such as work still to be done, revenue at risk, rehiring and extra attrition), with estimates labelled.
suggestions.reason: The 'such as' lists let a model with one leakage percentage and revenue at risk set to zero pass. For an industrial services group, consider requiring revenue at risk to be sized or given a break-even, and extra attrition to be costed.

suggestions.assertion: The reply compares the redundancy plan with alternatives that cost fewer jobs, on the same basis, before recommending.
suggestions.reason: Samples that only re-route the same 120 roles through attrition (B, C, J) pass on the same footing as samples that size non-headcount levers and leaders' pay on the same basis (A, D, F, H). A separate assertion on non-headcount levers and leaders going first would discriminate better.

suggestions.assertion: The reply keeps the numbers honest: restructuring is not presented as one-off when it recurs, assumptions are stated, and it shows sensitivities or a break-even.
suggestions.reason: The prompt gives no restructuring history, so 'not presented as one-off when it recurs' can only be tested where a sample addresses it explicitly (A, F, H); most samples pass on the other two clauses alone.

No assertion checks that the December announcement is reframed as a proposal opened for consultation (art. 25 WOR, §113 BetrVG exposure) or that the IAS 37 provision timing (FY2026 vs FY2027) is shown separately from cash; both separated strong from weak samples.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong on every assertion; the assertions do not separate this sample from the other top samples.
